name: sqlite_query
description: Run a read-only SQL query over a SQLite database file through Python's sqlite3 module and an authorizer that allows reading only (no write, ATTACH, extension or setting pragma), and return typed rows: an inline page (limit, and a byte ceiling) and, when the result is more, the whole of it as JSON Lines in rows_file. NULL is null, a BLOB is {blob_b64, length, sha256}, text that is not UTF-8 keeps its bytes. The database is opened immutable: a -wal or -shm beside it is inventoried (size, sha256, WAL frames) but NOT applied, so a row committed only in the WAL is missing from the result, which snapshot_status says; a hot rollback journal is said too. To read the state with the WAL applied, run sqlite_snapshot (it copies the set with hashes and has SQLite apply the WAL in the copy) and give its directory or its `database` as db_path: the answer then carries `snapshot` (what it holds, and whether the file queried still matches the receipt's sha256) and snapshot_status says which state the rows are; apply_wal is not a parameter here and asking for it is an error that names sqlite_snapshot. Several statements run one by one. A file that is not SQLite is reported with its first bytes (not in write_values mode) and entropy: high entropy is not identified, and encryption is one explanation among others. It does not recover deleted records or read unallocated pages. VALUES TO A FILE: with write_values true (only in a job run as secret output: the manifest's secret_output makes every job of this tool that sets write_values one, and the tool refuses a job whose process lacks SECRET_OUTPUT=1; refused outside a job before anything is opened) the tool takes table, and optionally columns, rowid_from and rowid_to, instead of sql, and writes the values of that one table to a 0600 file under $OUT (sqlite-query-values.jsonl, created exclusively and never followed through a link once the table is found and before its first row: a wrong name leaves nothing, a second export in the same job is refused as JSON; its last line is an end line, so a file cut short is recognisable) and puts none of them in the answer: the answer carries each cell's locator, type and length, per-column counts, the first rows, and locators_file with every row (bounded at 2 GiB, said). There is no sql in this mode on purpose: a WHERE, LIKE or JOIN over a column whose values are withheld would confirm a guess one call at a time, so the mode exports whole rows, reads them from the table itself (NOT INDEXED) in the table's own order, never in an index's (a WITHOUT ROWID table can be read through an index whose leading keys are its primary key, in the same order), and takes no filter; n_ranks names the columns whose values that order follows. What locates a row (table_kind): on an ordinary rowid table the rowid, which is no column's value (SQLite assigns it unless the application set it), in rowid order, and rowid_from/rowid_to select by it; on a table whose one primary key column is declared INTEGER and has no index of its own the rowid IS that column's value, so it is never printed, a rowid range is refused (rowid_is_a_value) and rows are located by their position n, which ranks the key's values; a WITHOUT ROWID table (whatever its columns are named) is ordered by its whole primary key with the key's collations and directions, so n ranks those values too; a rowid table whose columns named rowid, oid and _rowid_ hide the rowid is shadowed (n, in rowid order, or by its INTEGER PRIMARY KEY); a virtual table is located by n in its module's order, which can be a value's (fts5vocab's terms; n_ranks null), or is the named state virtual_table_unsupported on some SQLite builds. A virtual table is what SQLite's PRAGMA table_list says it is (where that pragma is missing: a table with no b-tree, or a statement whose words say VIRTUAL once its comments and quoted text are blanked), so a comment in its statement does not make it a rowid table. A WITHOUT ROWID table whose primary key names a collation this SQLite does not have (an application's own, such as Android's LOCALIZED) is read with a byte compare standing in for it, which sorts nothing: the rows come in the order the table stores them (collations_stood_in names it); a collation missing elsewhere in the schema makes the cells that need it unreadable, and a row with no readable cell for that reason stops the export as the named state missing_collation, not row_unreadable. An integer's length is the characters of its decimal form (its order of magnitude); a real's is its shortest repr, which is not. Nothing of a reading error is printed but what its code decides: sqlite's message, and the class Python gives an error whose message is not UTF-8, can quote a value, so every decision is taken on sqlite's result code (on Python before 3.11, on the text before the message's first quote matched whole against sqlite's fixed messages) and the class and the message go to the values file; a row that cannot be read whole is read alone, then a cell at a time with every readable cell in one query, and a cell over the 64 MiB length limit (value_too_large) or one sqlite cannot compute (unreadable) is listed and the export goes on (a row none of whose cells can be read stops it: row_unreadable); which cells are unreadable follows from the table's own expressions over its values. A write that fails (a full disk) ends the export as JSON with ok false, reason values_file_error and exit 1, and the answer's counts (values_file_holds, secret_values, cells_with_a_value: cells that hold a value) are read back from the kept file, which has no end line; a locators file that cannot be written leaves ok true and complete false. The values file stops at 2 GiB (values_file_stopped_at_row, and resume where a rowid range can go on), decided on the room each cell's line can take reckoned from its type and length alone (six bytes per byte of text, a BLOB's base64; an unreadable cell's room follows the length of sqlite's message), never on the bytes its value took, so where the file stops does not depend on how a value escapes; the run's time does, for values over about 1 MiB. No hash or fragment of a value is printed, and a printed file, table or column name shaped like a token is withheld. Only tables are read (not views). earlier_answers says how many other files answer the same question (a different answer is kept as name.2.jsonl, never over the first).

db_path.description: Path to the SQLite database file (the main file; a -wal beside it is reported, not applied), or the directory of a sqlite_snapshot, or the database inside one (its WAL is then applied in that copy).

sql.description: One or more SQL statements: SELECT, WITH, VALUES, EXPLAIN, or a PRAGMA that only reports. Required unless write_values is true, where it is refused.

csv.description: Render stdout, the text of the inline page, as CSV with a header (default: the shell's |-separated list without one).

limit.description: Rows in the inline page (default 100, at most 10000); the whole result is in rows_file when it is more. With write_values the page holds locators, and locators_file has every row.

max_seconds.description: Stop the query after this long (default 25, at most 110); the rows before it are kept and the result says it stopped.

readonly.description: Accepted only as true: this tool never opens a database for writing.

write_values.description: Write the values of one table to a 0600 file under $OUT instead of returning them (a job run as secret output, which the harness makes of a job that sets this; refused outside a job, and in a job whose process lacks SECRET_OUTPUT=1). Takes table, not sql. The answer carries locators, types, lengths and counts, never a value.

table.description: With write_values: the table whose cells go to the values file (a table, not a view).

columns.description: With write_values: the columns to export (default: every column of the table).

rowid_from.description: With write_values, on an ordinary rowid table (table_kind rowid): the first rowid to export (inclusive). The rowid there is no column's value; on a table whose rowid is a column's value (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), a WITHOUT ROWID or a virtual table a range is refused.

rowid_to.description: With write_values, on an ordinary rowid table: the last rowid to export (inclusive).
